#Module webcodecs

WebCodecs (src/page/bindings_webcodecs.odin, webcodecs_frame.odin): the pixel model, memory accounting and format conversions of a VideoFrame are native. The engine (native/js/runtime/web_webcodecs.c) holds the VideoFrame wrapper, builds the VideoFrameInit / VideoFrameBufferInit / VideoFrameCopyToOptions dictionaries, resolves copyTo's promise and transfers the handle in a postMessage. A VideoFrame is a host object (OBJECT_TAG); drawImage and createImageBitmap resolve it through the canvas image-source path. Decoders and encoders come in later modules.

Exposed to: Window, Worker. Source: api/webcodecs.widl.

WebCodecs VideoPixelFormat, in the order webcodecs_frame.odin's Frame_Format uses (format() returns -1 for a closed frame, which the engine maps to null).

#Functions

#VideoFrame_fromImage

VideoFrame VideoFrame_fromImage(u64 source, i64 timestamp, bool has_ts, i64 duration, bool has_duration) raises

///////////////////////////// new VideoFrame(image, init): build from a drawable source (an element handle img / canvas / video, or an object handle ImageBitmap / OffscreenCanvas / VideoFrame). The source's pixels are captured now. timestamp (microseconds) is required for a source without an intrinsic one; has_ts says it was given. Invalid_State when the source has no pixels (not loaded, empty, a GPU-only video), Quota when it is too large, Not_Supported when WebCodecs is off.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: VideoFrame_fromImage :: proc(c: ^Call, source: u64, timestamp: i64, has_ts: bool, duration: i64, has_duration: bool) -> (u64, Api_Error)

#VideoFrame_fromBuffer

VideoFrame VideoFrame_fromBuffer(bytes data, VideoPixelFormat format, i32 coded_w, i32 coded_h, i64 timestamp, i64 duration, bool has_duration, i32 vis_x, i32 vis_y, i32 vis_w, i32 vis_h, bool has_visible, i32 display_w, i32 display_h, bool has_display, i32[] layout_offsets, i32[] layout_strides, bool has_layout, i32 cp_prim, i32 cp_trans, i32 cp_matrix, i32 cp_full, i32 cp_has) raises

new VideoFrame(bufferSource, init): build from raw pixel bytes with a VideoFrameBufferInit. format, coded_w, coded_h and timestamp are required (the engine checks). has_visible / has_display carry the optional visibleRect and displaySize; a custom plane layout gives layout_offsets / layout_strides (one per plane) when has_layout. Colour space members are -1 when absent; cp_has says a colorSpace was given at all.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: VideoFrame_fromBuffer :: proc(c: ^Call, data: []u8, format: Api_VideoPixelFormat, coded_w: i32, coded_h: i32, timestamp: i64, duration: i64, has_duration: bool, vis_x: i32, vis_y: i32, vis_w: i32, vis_h: i32, has_visible: bool, display_w: i32, display_h: i32, has_display: bool, layout_offsets: []i32, layout_strides: []i32, has_layout: bool, cp_prim: i32, cp_trans: i32, cp_matrix: i32, cp_full: i32, cp_has: i32) -> (u64, Api_Error)

#VideoFrame_allocationSize

i32 VideoFrame_allocationSize(VideoFrame frame, i32 format, i32 rx, i32 ry, i32 rw, i32 rh, bool has_rect, i32[] layout_offsets, i32[] layout_strides, bool has_layout) raises

///////////////////////////// frame.allocationSize(options): the bytes copyTo needs. format -1 keeps the frame's own; has_rect gives a crop rectangle; a custom layout's strides are honoured when has_layout.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: VideoFrame_allocationSize :: proc(c: ^Call, frame: Api_VideoFrame, format: i32, rx: i32, ry: i32, rw: i32, rh: i32, has_rect: bool, layout_offsets: []i32, layout_strides: []i32, has_layout: bool) -> (i32, Api_Error)

#VideoFrame_copyTo

i32 VideoFrame_copyTo(VideoFrame frame, out bytes dst, i32 format, i32 rx, i32 ry, i32 rw, i32 rh, bool has_rect, i32[] in_offsets, i32[] in_strides, bool has_layout) raises

frame.copyTo(destination, options): copies the frame (or its crop rectangle) into dst as format (-1 = own). The plane layout used is kept on the frame (read it with VideoFrame_copyLayout); the return is the plane count. The engine wraps this in a promise resolving to a PlaneLayout[]. Range for a rectangle outside the picture, Not_Supported for an unsupported conversion, Invalid_State for a closed frame.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: VideoFrame_copyTo :: proc(c: ^Call, frame: Api_VideoFrame, dst: []u8, format: i32, rx: i32, ry: i32, rw: i32, rh: i32, has_rect: bool, in_offsets: []i32, in_strides: []i32, has_layout: bool) -> (i32, Api_Error)

#VideoFrame_transfer

VideoFrame VideoFrame_transfer(VideoFrame frame, u32 owner) raises

postMessage transfer within one realm: move the pixels into a new object (owner = the receiving realm's instance), closing the original. Data_Clone when it is already detached.

Raises: returns an Error (see web).

Host: VideoFrame_transfer :: proc(c: ^Call, frame: Api_VideoFrame, owner: u32) -> (u64, Api_Error)

#VideoFrame_takeForTransfer

u64 VideoFrame_takeForTransfer(VideoFrame frame)

Cross-realm transfer (postMessage to a worker): the source realm detaches the frame into a process-wide token; the destination realm adopts it. The pixels stay host-owned throughout. Both are used by structured clone (native/js/runtime/clone.c). takeForTransfer returns 0 when the frame is already closed; adoptTransfer returns 0 when the token is unknown or the destination is over its memory budget.

Host: VideoFrame_takeForTransfer :: proc(c: ^Call, frame: Api_VideoFrame) -> u64
